verdict.rationale: FireHydrant gives each incident an internal status page that needs no auth or license. Updates posted via `/fh update` or Command Center appear there, and AI summaries can be tailored by Audience for different stakeholder groups. That covers structured updates without joining the war room, but no self-service subscription mechanism for stakeholders is documented; only admin-configured Runbook posts to Slack channels are shown. missing for 10: documented stakeholder self-subscribe/follow for incident updates (e.g., email or Slack subscription by the stakeholder), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, internal stakeholders get structured incident updates they can subscribe to, without joining the war room

citations.quote: All incident notes/updates posted via Slack (`/fh update`) or via Command Center are posted to the Internal Status Page
For public (to your organization) incidents, these internal status pages do not require auth or a FireHydrant license to view.
With our new Audiences feature, summaries can now be tailored to meet the specific needs of different stakeholder groups.
Universal Access: Available to everyone in your Slack workspace, they don't need a FireHydrant account.
We'll use our runbook to then add a step with conditions for posting into Slack when a new summary has become available.
